name: Chandrayaan-1
short_status: Mission ended Aug 29, 2009 (IST) when contact was lost 312 days in, with about 95% of objectives met; JPL ground radar located the derelict orbiter still circling at about 200 km in 2016-17.
tagline: ISRO · India · Orbiter · 2008 · The quiet decades Success
stats: instruments from India, the US, the UK, Germany, Sweden and Bulgaria
in lunar orbit, of a planned two years

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 22 October 2008, 00:52 UT, on PSLV-XL (flight C11) from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota

facts.label: Spacecraft
facts.value: 1,380 kg at launch, 700 W of power, designed for two years in a 100 km circular polar orbit

facts.label: Mission cost
facts.value: About Rs 3.8 billion (roughly $78 million at launch), which BBC noted was considerably less than Japan's and China's 2007 lunar orbiters

facts.label: Instruments
facts.value: 11 from six countries: five Indian (TMC, HySI, LLRI, HEX and the Moon Impact Probe) plus NASA's M3 and Mini-SAR, the UK-led C1XS, Germany's SIR-2, Sweden's SARA and Bulgaria's RADOM

facts.label: Moon Impact Probe
facts.value: A 35 kg box carrying a descent camera, a radar altimeter and the CHACE mass spectrometer, with the Indian flag painted on its side panels; released 14 November 2008, it struck near Shackleton crater at 15:01 UT

facts.label: Impact site (refined 2021)
facts.value: About 89.55 S, 122.93 W, on the Earth-facing slope of the Connecting Ridge between Shackleton and De Gerlache craters; earlier published estimates (89.76 S, 39.40 W in the UN registration; 89.54 S, 44.71 W in ISRO's 2015 atlas) differ, and the crater itself has never been found in LROC images

facts.label: M3 water discovery
facts.value: OH and H2O absorption near 3 micrometers detected across sunlit soils, strongest toward the poles; published in Science online 24 September 2009 (Pieters et al.), alongside corroborating Cassini VIMS and Deep Impact observations

facts.label: CHACE water vapor
facts.value: The Moon Impact Probe's mass spectrometer measured water vapor in the thin sunlit lunar ambience during its 25-minute descent on 14 November 2008; the peer-reviewed result appeared in Planetary and Space Science in 2010 (Sridharan et al.)

facts.label: Mini-SAR polar ice
facts.value: Radar signatures consistent with water ice found in more than 40 small permanently shadowed craters (2 to 15 km) near the north pole, announced March 2010; NASA's estimate was at least 600 million metric tons

facts.label: Mission end
facts.value: Last contact at 20:00 UT on 28 August 2009 (01:30 IST August 29, the date ISRO uses); NASA credits the mission with at least 95% of its objectives

facts.label: On-orbit tally
facts.value: 312 days in lunar orbit, more than 3,400 orbits of the Moon and over 70,000 images returned

facts.label: Found again (2017)
facts.value: JPL beamed microwaves at the Moon from the 70 m Goldstone dish and caught echoes at Green Bank: the derelict crossed the beam on 2 July 2016, still in a roughly 200 km polar orbit circling every 2 hours 8 minutes; announced 9 March 2017

timeline: Launched at 00:52 UT on PSLV-C11 from Sriharikota, the first flight of the uprated PSLV-XL
Enters lunar orbit: India's first spacecraft at the Moon
Reaches its 100 km circular polar mapping orbit
Moon Impact Probe strikes near Shackleton crater at 15:01 UT after a roughly 25-minute descent, imaging and sampling the exosphere all the way down
Star tracker fails; ISRO flies on with gyroscopes plus antenna-pointing data and landmark imaging
Orbit raised from 100 km to 200 km for wider-swath imaging and lunar gravity studies
Contact lost abruptly (20:00 UT Aug 28; 01:30 IST Aug 29); the mission ends after 312 days
The M3 water and hydroxyl result is published online in Science and announced by NASA
Mar 2010
Mini-SAR results announced: ice signatures in 40-plus shadowed north polar craters
CHACE's in-descent water vapor measurement is published in Planetary and Space Science
The derelict physically crosses a Goldstone-Green Bank radar beam above the lunar north pole, proving it is still in orbit (announced 9 Mar 2017)
Aug 2018
M3 data yields the first direct evidence of exposed water ice inside polar cold traps (Li et al., PNAS)
Mar 2021
LPSC analysis relocates the Moon Impact Probe's impact point to the Connecting Ridge slope at about 89.55 S, 122.93 W
